page: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the n1 server family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon processor cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is configured with 30.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes hardware support for AVX, AES cryptography, and FMA instructions, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations place the n1-standard-8 in the lower-to-average performance tiers. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests, such as stress-ng and Geekbench, return weak to poor ratings, with a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and a multi-core score of 3531.0. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is average, measuring 45.37 GB/sec for read operations and 34.65 GB/sec for write operations, whereas small-block cached read bandwidth is weak at 324.06 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates average performance in specific workloads like Geekbench ray tracing and small-model LLM text generation, but falls into the weak category for database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n1-standard-8 offers a balanced resource allocation profile without the premium cost of specialized compute or memory-optimized hardware. However, the tradeoff is its reliance on older Intel Xeon architecture, which limits its execution speed in modern instruction-heavy tasks. This instance is suitable for moderate general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, light database operations, and development environments that do not require high-speed local storage or GPU acceleration.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-standard-8 is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 30.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.3 GHz. It provides a balanced 1:3.75 vCPU-to-memory ratio but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate weak single-core and multi-core CPU capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 923.0 and multi-core score of 3531.0. Large-block memory bandwidth is average, reaching 45.37 GB/sec for reads, while database and static web serving throughput remain in the lower tiers. Qualitatively, this instance offers a cost-effective option for legacy workloads and development environments where high-density compute is unnecessary. It is best utilized for general-purpose applications, basic web serving, and moderate multi-threaded tasks.
